KEY MESSAGE 1...Strong/long duration Nor'easter will bring damaging 
wind gusts, coastal flooding/beach erosion, and periods of heavy 
rain this weekend. Power outages are a concern especially CT/RI as 
well as eastern MA. Rain/gusty winds persist into Mon. 

The overall forecast theme remains on track...although the track has 
shifted a bit further to the southwest. An anomalous low pressure 
system for September will intensity off the mid-Atlantic coast over 
the next 24 hours. In fact...the NAEFS situational awareness display 
indicates this low pressure system is outside of the models 
climatology for this time of year. This has been the signal 
indicating that this would be an impactful/long duration Nor'easter 
for our region. The low will initially retrograde towards the mid-
Atlantic coast before slowly moving northeast and weakening through 
early next week. The above supports a strong/long duration 
Nor'easter that we have been discussing for quite sometime now. 
We will break this down more below. 

1) Strong to Damaging Wind Gusts... 

The biggest concern with this storm will be strong NE winds. This is 
especially true since the winds will be of both long duration and 
also coupled with heavy rain/fully leafed trees. This will 
exacerbate the risk for tree damage and power outages if this same 
storm were occurring a few months later. While the track over the 
past 24-36 hours has shifted further southwest...the gradient will 
still be strong enough to result in a long period of strong to 
damaging NE wind gusts especially CT/RI/eastern MA. The strongest of 
the winds will arrive across the Cape/Islands later tonight with a 
northeast LLJ of 55-65 knots. This northeast LLJ slowly lifts west 
Sat into early Sun...so the specific timing of the strongest winds 
will differ in time. 

We are thinking much of the immediate coast will see NE wind gusts 
of 45-60 mph especially near the south coast. A few gusts of 65-70 
mph not out of the question towards Block Island closer to the core 
of the LLJ which will be tracking to our southwest. Whether or not 
places hit specific high wind criteria is less important that the 
long duration of the NE winds combined with the fully leafed trees. 
High Wind Warnings continue along the coast into early Sunday 
morning. Further inland...we are expecting NE wind gusts of 35 to 50 
mph strongest of which may be in our CT zones closer to the 
Nor'easter/s circulation. Given the fully leafed trees combined with 
long duration of the event...the Wind Advisory continues. 
Overall...the wind and tree damage/power outage risk will be the 
biggest impact for most people. 

2) Beach Erosion/Coastal Flooding...

The other big issue with this storm will be the beach 
erosion/coastal flooding issues over multiple high tide cycles. 
While this will not be a storm under-going rapid bombogenesis...the 
persistence of these strong NE winds and high seas offshore are 
concerning. A storm surge on the order of 1 to 2 feet and perhaps 
briefly near 2.5 feet are expected through the weekend along east 
face ocean exposed beaches. Coastal Flood Warnings continue along 
the eastern MA coast including the Cape/Islands through the weekend. 
This along with 15 to 25 foot seas offshore will result in minor 
coastal flooding with a few pockets of low end moderate coastal 
flooding possible during each high tide cycle this weekend. The 
biggest issue looks to be severe beach erosion given long duration 
of strong NE wind gusts with the high seas offshore. Astronomical 
high tides are increasing through the weekend...so even as winds 
eventually start to slowly diminish these issues will be a concern. 
Given this event will impact multiple high tide cycles...the water 
may struggle to drain out after each high tide. Heavy rainfall may 
also exacerbate these issues a well. Overall...the biggest impact 
from this system may be in regards to beach erosion given such a 
long duration event. 

Coastal Flood Advisories continue for the south coasts of RI and MA. 
ALthough the NE winds will be somewhat of a mitigating factor...very 
large swell from the Nor'easter to our south will send large swell 
northward. In addition...pressure falls will also aid in water level 
rises. So we do expect pockets of splashover/minor coastal flooding 
along with minor beach erosion through the weekend. 

3) Bulk of the Steady/Heavier Rain Sat afternoon through Mon...

An initial area of rain near the south coast will lift northwest 
tonight. However...drier air to the north will result in the 
activity becoming more scattered and showery as it lifts near and 
especially northwest of the I-95 corridor. While there will be some 
scattered showers across...much of this time may feature dry weather 
with the initial rain focused towards the southeast New England 
coast. The heaviest rain for most locations will not be until Sat 
afternoon but will continue right through Mon.
